goal: Close the four blocking defects a DeepSeek Harness documentation audit found in the DSH bundle: child-process credential leakage, a predictable state-write temp file, ignored exec.signal, and an unmanaged/unconfined git child.

alignment.evidence: Branch fix/dsh-audit-blocking cut from main fd84841; Project Harness bundle only, no product code.
Three parallel doc-audit agents covered all 112 remaining English docs (30,884 lines) with file:line citations; each of the four defects was then confirmed by reading the source before any edit.
ADR-0006 records the four defects, the shared-module constraint (the CLI has no Cordis context), and why the seam is optional rather than injected.

Read-only git probe, one workspace file, plus in-process signal handling. vcs-control.js, project-handoff.js and the legacy experiment scripts were deliberately left alone. No merge, release or deployment.

scripts/child-env.js owns the scrub rule, scripts/git-probe.js the argv table and local runner, dsh/skills/git.js the shell runner, dsh/skills/state.js the write, and the manifest decides which runner is used.

Only the four blocking findings, plus the tests and docs they require. The three remaining audit improvements (ctx.fs write seam, bundle config row, per-scope tool restriction) are explicitly out of scope.

No new dependency; the shell package is never imported. One scrub rule mirrored from the harness seam rather than invented, one frozen argv table, and no new abstraction beyond the two runner factories.

Node 22.23.2: 124/124 tests; dsh:verify 39 integration + 174 conformance checks against a real DeepSeek Harness checkout; skills:verify, skills:catalog --check, control:verify, memory:resume and git diff --check all pass. Six guards were each proven red on their reintroduced regression and green after reverting.
